Our actions can have terrible consequences even if we didn’t have any evil intentions.
Böse Kinder kriegen nichts vom Sankt Nikolaus.
Naughty children don’t get anything from St. Nicholas.
mean, dark (of jokes, satire, tricks, etc.)

Boson.et: From English boson, from Bose + -on. Named after Indian Bengali physicist and polymath Satyendra Nath Bose; coined by British theoretical physicist Paul Dirac in a lecture titled "Developments in Atomic Theory".

Böse.et: From Middle High German bōse, from Old High German bōsi. Cognate with English boast.

Bosporus.et: From Latin Bosporus, from Ancient Greek Βόσπορος (Bósporos).

boshaft.et: Ultimately from an umlaut-less byform of böse (compare also erbosen) + -haft, taking the place of earlier boshaftig.

s:

s: rude awakening (a spontaneous realization that one's previous assumptions (or illusions) were false)
Der 24. Februar war ein böses Erwachen für ganz Europa.

Sie halten sie gefangen und schlagen sie tot in digitalen Szenarien.
 Böse Zungen behaupten, sie täten dies aufgrund minimaler Genitalien.

They hold [time] captive and kill it in digital scenarios.
 Mockers claim that they do this by reason of miminal genitalia.
böse Zungen.et: Literally, “evil tongues”, perhaps after French mauvaises langues. Compare Dutch boze tongen.

s: bad blood (feelings of hostility or ill will)
Lebt ich dazu, / Ein Scherz nur und Gelächter meinem Brutus / Zu sein, wenn Gram und böses Blut mich plagt?
Hath Cassius lived / To be but mirth and laughter to his Brutus, / When grief and blood ill-tempered vexeth him?
[Dromio von Syracus.] Bey meiner Six, es giebt böse Buben in eurer Stadt.
By my troth, your town is troubled with unruly boys.
